name: Rolf Haugen
languages: Norwegian (his grandfather's, enough to read the oldest pages of the co-op minutes)
equipment: Heavy coat: a co-op feed-store barn jacket, canvas with a corduroy collar, HOLLOW FORK CO-OP on the back
Wood axe, in the truck's tool box
Hunting rifle: a .30-06 his grandfather bought him for his sixteenth birthday, the same night his father told him about the Book
Work clothes, leather gloves, and a red kerchief he has never once pulled up over his mouth
The keys to the co-op grain trucks, the elevator, the feed mill and the office
The combination to the Diebold safe, which is his mother's birthday, 4-11-21, and which he has never written down
A letter of reference from the University of Wisconsin–River Falls dairy farm, where he worked two summers
A CB radio in the grain truck: handle Little Elevator
features: Up Before Dawn (Farm-Raised origin: he needs only 6 hours for a long rest and can't be surprised while awake in the last hour before sunrise; advantage on saves against exhaustion from hard work, cold and lost sleep; he notices without a check when animals are frightened, sick or behaving wrongly)

Hard to Kill (Roughneck: once per long rest, when reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, he drops to 1 instead; he ignores his first level of exhaustion and has advantage on CON saves against exhaustion, cold and hard labor)

Heavy Work (Roughneck: advantage on STR checks to lift, push, pull, break or force something; he counts as one size larger for what he can carry, drag or lift, and can carry an unconscious adult at full speed)

Bull-Headed (Roughneck, 2nd level: once per short rest, when he fails a fear check, he gains no Dread, but on his next turn must move toward the source and attack it or break what stands between them, or smash something nearby)
Trade: Teamster (Roughneck, 3rd level: he is already proficient in Driving, and has advantage on Driving checks to keep a vehicle on the road or get a stalled one started under pressure)

Hired On (Farmhand background: at any farm in the county he can get a meal and a place in the barn for a day's work, and farm people talk to him as an equal; he notices without a check when a farm's rhythm is wrong: chores undone, stock unfed, a field nobody will work)

personality.traits: I am quiet, slow to speak and quick to work. I know every man in Hollow Fork by his voice on the radio and his walk across a yard. I eat lunch alone in the truck.
personality.ideals: A town is the people in it, and a co-op is supposed to be everybody holding each other up. Not this.
personality.bonds: My father, who is drowning and who I love. My mother, Anna, who died in 1970 not knowing. Hollow Fork, every field of it. And the girl in the Fossums' hired man's house, whom I carried groceries to and could not look at.
personality.flaws: I have known since I was sixteen and said nothing for eight years. I am a coward who is about to stop being one, and I am not sure what I will break when I do.

appearance: Twenty-four, big and fair, with a sunburned neck, a broken nose from high-school football, enormous careful hands, a co-op jacket and a seed cap, and the eyes of a man who has not slept properly in a month.
backstory: Rolf Haugen is the only son of Harald Haugen, manager of the Hollow Fork Farmers' Cooperative, and the great-grandson of Gunnar Haugen, who wrote the terms of 1904. He grew up in the elevator and the feed mill, played fullback for the Hollow Fork Harvesters, spent two years at the ag school in River Falls and came home in 1972 to drive the co-op's grain trucks and learn the business, because one day it will be his. On the night of his sixteenth birthday his father took him to the co-op office, opened the safe and showed him the Book, and told him that one day the pen would be his too. Rolf has not slept well since. He has watched the guests come every September: a hunter last year, whom he liked; this year a girl with a peace sign on her knapsack, whose groceries he carried to the Fossums' hired man's house. He knows the safe combination, the night man's rounds and every voice on channel 14. He has been waiting, without knowing it, for someone from outside to give him a reason.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Rolf is the party's door into the co-op and the Book in hs-scenario-002, its guide and voice on the night of the corn in hs-scenario-003 (he knows every man in the line by voice and can call them off by name across the creek), and a speaker for the house of Haugen at the Cold Hole in hs-scenario-004. He joins when shown proof (the back room, Dawn's Polaroids, the pencilled name) or caught alone and spoken to straight. He is strong, steady, and not a talker; give him one or two lines a scene and make them count. He will not hurt a Hollow Fork man, and he will stand between the party and one. He loves his father and will defend him to anyone, including the party, until the end.
dmNotes.voice: Slow, low, few words, a Wisconsin farm accent, 'yeah, no' and 'you bet', long silences. On the radio, Little Elevator, easy and friendly. When he finally says what he knows, it comes out flat and fast, like a man reading a grain price.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: never write a name. Secondary: save his father, from the Book or from the second door. Tertiary: keep Hollow Fork alive afterward, whatever that takes.
dmNotes.secrets: He knows what the second door is. His father told him that night, too: 'If it ever has to stop and they won't stop it, it stops with me. Not you.' Rolf has dreaded Harvest Days every year since. He also knows that in 1951 his grandfather, Sigurd Haugen, led the men on the Fork bridge road behind Einar Aldahl's Hudson, and that his grandfather wept about it when he was dying.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: wary, then loyal, steadily. Toward his father: love and anger. Toward Arnie Fossum: he grew up in his kitchen. Toward Marit Lunde: cold. Toward Ingeborg: she taught him to read Norwegian, from the co-op's oldest minutes.
